- The standard procedure and estimated wall-clock time for a full tenant destruction (including snapshots, backups, and any cached/prefetch layers).
- Evidence types we can accept for verification (logs, manifest of deleted snapshot ids, signed runbook entry).

Hi Gil — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise package to get this over the line (see attachments). High-level summary below and proposed next steps.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Territorial lock: tenants are bound to a region by routing, storage placement, and tenant-aware network ACLs. We utilize region-scoped routing tables + per-tenant placement tags so compute and primary storage are pinned to the selected region. Backups are configured on a per-tenant policy: default is same-region snapshot; cross-region replication only happens if explicitly enabled for that tenant.
- Deletion window: full automated wipe path (running from our orchestration service) completes in two phases — logical data purge (minutes to hours depending on queue), then snapshot lifecycle deletion (can take up to 72 hours to finalize deletion and overwrite on some storage tiers).
- Evidence we provide: runbook execution ID, deletion-manifest (snapshot ids), time-stamped audit logs, and cryptographic key rotation confirmation when requested.
- Exceptions: emergency cross-region replication is off by default; if enabled we enumerate replicas and include their destruction in the manifest.

Attached: redwood-erase-playbook.pdf (executable steps + acceptance checklist), site-separation-diagram.png (placement diagram).

Next steps:
1) Ben and I will drop the wipe script and verification artifacts into a shared Drive link and send the runbook outputs for a sample tenant purge.
2) Laura will outline attestation language for legal sign-off and a short DocuSign flow.
3) If your team wants, we can run a live destroy rehearsal on a non-prod tenant and share the full manifest.

I cc'd Ben and Laura. Ben — can you add the script + sample log bundle? Laura — want to propose simple attestation text for FinServe to sign?

Thanks,

Gil / Vanessa / team — adding the operational detail below and attaching the runbook snippets.

Operational detail (concise):
- Placement: Orchestrator tags (tenant_id, region_code) drive scheduler constraints; at provisioning we write a placement record that the scheduler and the storage allocator honor. Primary storage volumes are created with region-local affinity and a tenant tag.
- Routing / Isolation: Control plane enforces per-tenant VPC-like network isolation using region-scoped routing and security groups. No cross-region peering for tenant traffic unless explicitly requested in the customer's account profile.
- Snapshot lifecycle: Snapshots created by the storage system are GC'd through a retention policy. When a tenant deletion is initiated the system marks snapshots for immediate tombstoning and sets TTL=0, then submits deletion jobs. Deletions traverse storage-backend queues and we surface a deletion-manifest with snapshot ids + deletion timestamps when jobs complete.
- KMS: Each tenant uses an envelope key; when a tenant is destroyed we either rotate or schedule key destruction depending on customer preference. We will provide signed key-rotation logs or key-destruction attestations.

Attachments included in this message (stubs):
- wipe-script.sh (automation used to start the workflow)
- wipe-runbook.md (sample run output + expected manifest format)

Sample verification artifacts we will provide in the Drive link:
- deletion-manifest.json (list of snapshot ids + timestamps)
- audit.log excerpt (time-range showing orchestration steps)
- control-plane event ids (for cross-reference)

Notes on timing: logical purge typically completes within an hour for average-sized tenants; snapshot chain teardown is bounded by backend GC (we guarantee deletion manifest within 72 hours). If you need faster finality we can arrange expedited cleanup on a committed SLA.

Ben Carter

Hi Gil — attaching a short attestation template (attestation-docusign.pdf) and proposing acceptance criteria below. Once you confirm the criteria we can execute the DocuSign flow and provide the evidence bundle.

Proposed acceptance criteria (FinServe sign-off):
1) Placement proof: site separation diagram + orchestration placement record for a sample tenant id (time-stamped).
2) Execution proof: deletion-manifest signed by our orchestration service (manifest includes snapshot ids, deletion job ids, and timestamps).
3) Cryptographic proof: KMS rotation or destruction log for tenant envelope key tied to the deletion manifest id.
4) Audit trail: control-plane logs for the deletion operation (30-day retention of the relevant slice) and link to Drive evidence.
5) SLA confirmation: Redwood will guarantee an evidence package (manifest + logs) within 72 hours of a deletion request; optional expedited 24-hour evidence on contract.

If those five items look good to FinServe we'll start the DocuSign attestation and run a rehearsal on a non-prod tenant and share the full Drive link (see related links).
